Pre-Incorporation & Know-Your-Customer

UBO Ultimate Beneficial Owner Screening Rules Official Registry Only

>=25% ownership / control

Applicable AML statute: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo; Real Decreto 304/2014, de 5 de mayo, por el que se aprueba el Reglamento de la Ley 10/2010; Real Decreto-ley 7/2021, de 27 de abril, por el que se crea el Registro Central de Titularidades Reales (Central Register of Ultimate Beneficial Owners); Order JUS/319/2022, de 11 de abril, on the functioning of the Central Register of Ultimate Beneficial Owners.
Registered Agent & Physical Address Licensed Agent Required

A Spanish SL must maintain a registered office (domicilio social) in Spain that is real and suitable for receiving service of legal process and exercising corporate functions. A virtual office may be used for administrative correspondence and mail-forwarding, but a mere virtual mailbox registered as the sole fiscal establishment creates significant substance risks in tax audits, transfer-pricing reviews, and AML/CFT controls. For an outsourced virtual CFO consultancy, the virtual office is acceptable only where the company maintains actual management, decision-making, personnel, and operational infrastructure in Spain; otherwise tax authorities may rebut the Spanish tax residence and deny treaty benefits.

✓ Partner licensed company-secretary channels provide local registered address and government mail forwarding.

Stage 02

Statutory Formation & Board Resolutions

Competent registry, governing statute, capital lockup rules, and first board resolution template.

Competent corporate registry

Registro Mercantil Central for name certification and the Provincial Commercial Registry of the registered office for statutory inscription; a Spanish notary public executes the public deed.

Governing statute

Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010, of 2 July, approving the revised text of the Capital Companies Act (Ley de Sociedades de Capital), Articles 19-24 on incorporation deed and articles of association, Article 22 on registered office, Articles 23 and 24 on registration and publicity, Articles 58-62 on administrators, and Articles 404 and 443 on share capital of the Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada.

Formation / constitutional filings

Public deed of incorporation (escritura pública de constitución) filed for inscription in the Mercantile Registry (inscripción registral).

Incorporation processing time

⚡ 23 business days (SOP sum)

Paid-up Capital & Blocked Account Regime Mandatory Capital Deposit & Lockup

Minimum share capital EUR 3,000 fully subscribed and fully paid in cash or in kind before execution of the deed; no statutory escrow lock-up is required beyond full payment, evidenced by a blocked bank capital deposit certificate.

Funding & unlock path: Fire safety and evacuation certification for office occupancy under Royal Decree 513/2017, structural load and building occupancy suitability certificate from municipal technical services, and mandatory occupational health and safety risk assessment under Law 31/1995 and related workplace regulations.

Paid-in capital rule: Minimum share capital EUR 3,000 fully subscribed and fully paid in cash or in kind before execution of the deed; no statutory escrow lock-up is required beyond full payment, evidenced by a blocked bank capital deposit certificate.

Stage 03

Tax Identity & Indirect Tax

Tax authority e-portal, entity tax classification elections, VAT thresholds, and 0% export documentation chain.

Tax ID Application Infrastructure

Competent tax authority

Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) — Sede Electrónica: https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es

E-government filing portal

Pre-incorporation: file Modelo 030 with the notarial draft of the SL deeds to obtain a provisional NIF from AEAT. Execute the incorporation deed before a Spanish notary, pay the corresponding deed and registration taxes, and file the deed at the Registro Mercantil. After registration, file Modelo 036 (Censo de Empresarios) at AEAT to formalize the definitive NIF and VAT/IVA registration, with the final VAT ID shown as ES+NIF. Non-resident incorporators/officers need a NIE or must appoint an AEAT tax representative.

Tax ID type & application path: Entity_Level_Taxation — Pre-incorporation: file Modelo 030 with the notarial draft of the SL deeds to obtain a provisional NIF from AEAT. Execute the incorporation deed before a Spanish notary, pay the corresponding deed and registration taxes, and file the deed at the Registro Mercantil. After registration, file Modelo 036 (Censo de Empresarios) at AEAT to formalize the definitive NIF and VAT/IVA registration, with the final VAT ID shown as ES+NIF. Non-resident incorporators/officers need a NIE or must appoint an AEAT tax representative.

Default Tax Classification & Elections

Default tax classification

Entity_Level_Taxation

Available election forms

No check-the-box regime exists in Spain; the SL is automatically a corporate taxpayer. Available elections include the group consolidation regime for Spanish groups holding 75% or more of subsidiaries and special joint-venture modalities (UTEs). Hybrid-mismatch and ATAD anti-abuse rules are mandatory and non-elective; no domestic hybrid election is available.

VAT / GST & 0% Export Zero-Rating

Standard VAT / GST rate

21%

Mandatory registration threshold (Nexus)

No local turnover threshold: VAT registration is compulsory before the first taxable supply in Spain. For intra-EU distance sales by EU suppliers, the special OSS threshold is EUR 10,000; non-EU suppliers have no threshold.

Export 0% zero-rating conditions

Goods exports to non-EU destinations qualify for the 0% export exemption under LIVA Article 21 if physical dispatch or transport to a non-EU country is evidenced. For cross-border services (fractional CFO and bookkeeping) supplied to a non-EU-established client, the supply is outside the scope of Spanish VAT under Article 69 LIVA place-of-supply rules, thereby producing no Spanish VAT charge; when supplied to an EU VAT-registered client, the reverse-charge mechanism applies and the transaction is not zero-rated locally.

  • Customs export declaration (DUI — Documento Único Administrativo)
  • Bill of Lading (B/L) or Air Waybill evidencing physical departure from the EU plus proof of customs exit
  • Commercial invoice or detailed service contract identifying the foreign customer and the actual service rendered
  • Inward remittance certificate (SWIFT MT103 or bank transfer evidence) showing receipt of non-resident payment
  • Proof of the customer's non-EU/EU status including, where applicable, a valid EU VAT identification number with VIES confirmation

AEAT uses the SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) near-real-time VAT clearance system for taxpayers whose annual turnover exceeds EUR 6,000,000, with electronic transmission of invoice records to AEAT within 4–8 days via authenticated web services/API. Verifactu-certified billing software (RD 1007/2023) is mandatory for software-issued invoices, requiring tamper-proof sequential hash records and accessible AEAT-compatible event logs. Private B2B interoperable electronic invoicing under the Crea y Crece law is being phased in for all Spanish-established businesses; public-sector invoices use Facturae XML.

Ex post AEAT controls verify export evidence; non-compliant claims are reassessed at 21% IVA plus late interest under LGT Articles 26–27 and are subject to penalty scales in LGT Articles 191–192 (50%–150% of the amount, with 150% reserved for concealment or fraud). Fraudulent zero-rating above EUR 120,000 per tax period triggers criminal tax fraud prosecution (Delito contra la Hacienda Pública), public-contract debarment, and retrospective clawback of all claimed credit or refunds.

Stage 04

Banking & Treasury Architecture

Central-bank FX diagnosis, tier-1 local banks vs offshore digital EMI matrix, and KYC rejection defense guide.

Foreign Exchange Regime & Central Bank Policy

Current-account convertibility

Spain has full currency convertibility for both current and capital account transactions under Articles 63 to 66 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union. There are no general exchange controls, no prior authorisation requirements for profit repatriation, and no differentiated FX approval regime for non-resident investors. Dividend and profit remittances to non-resident shareholders are processed freely by commercial banks once Spanish corporate tax compliance is verified, fiscal representation requirements are met, and any applicable treaty withholding or domestic 19% non-resident withholding tax is settled. Practical hurdles include anti-money-laundering source-of-funds verification, bank de-risking of smaller corporate structures, Form 720 asset declaration obligations for non-resident holdings by Spanish tax-resident directors, and transfer pricing/beneficial ownership substance requirements where the Spanish SL is part of a multinational group.

Export proceeds surrender rules

Spain does not impose mandatory surrender, forced conversion, or repatriation timelines for export proceeds. Export receivables may be denominated in EUR or in freely convertible or non-convertible currencies and may be retained in domestic foreign-currency accounts or offshore operating accounts. The remaining obligations are statistical and regulatory: cross-border payment operations exceeding EUR 12,500 must be reported to Banco de España under the balance-of-payments reporting framework on the applicable monthly or quarterly cycle; annual declaration of foreign assets over EUR 50,000 per asset class is due by 31 March on Form 720; Intrastat declarations are required for intra-EU goods traffic, and Spanish customs export documentation must be retained as underlying evidence. The statutory expectation is accurate supporting documentation rather than fixed conversion ratios or surrender percentages.

Central bank supervision: Banco de España (Bank of Spain) as national competent authority for monetary policy, financial stability, payment systems, statistics and AML/CFT supervision; regulatory policy coordinated with the European Central Bank and the European Banking Authority.

Offshore Digital Bank / EMI Whitelist

Wise Fit: High

Medium to High, subject to PSD2 and Banco de España supervision. EEA-authorised electronic money institutions and payment institutions can provide IBANs, multi-currency wallets, payout services and SWIFT-like rails through passporting, but they are not eligible substitutes for a statutory credit institution account when bank confirmation for capital increases or documentary trade credits is required. Cross-border EMIs such as Wise for business may serve payroll to foreign contractors, vendor disbursements, and collection waterfall accounts, but the primary corporate current account for tax, creditor protection, and SL statutory capital contributions should remain at a fully licensed credit institution. Any EMI arrangement must preserve segregated customer funds, include Spanish language and consumer protection disclosures, and cannot offer deposit-taking or credit products.

Core KYC Rejection Triggers & Defense Dossier

Ultimate beneficial ownership above 25% is opaque, layered through multiple intermediaries or holding companies

Root cause: Ultimate beneficial ownership above 25% is opaque, layered through multiple intermediaries or holding companies

Defense evidence: Current Spanish commercial registry certificate, UBO declaration in the statutory form, share register extract, ownership chain chart from each intermediary, notarised passports of all natural-person UBOs, corporate article details, certificate of good standing from foreign registries, and written explanation of the commercial rationale for the holding structure.
Politically exposed person or family member of a PEP is a shareholder, director, or authorised signatory

Root cause: Politically exposed person or family member of a PEP is a shareholder, director, or authorised signatory

Defense evidence: Explicit PEP status declaration, detailed source-of-wealth report, audited or tax-filed financial statements, independent wealth verification, bank statements covering the funding path, notarised employment and business asset documentation, external compliance sign-off by the SL's in-house or external AML officer, and confirmation of no adverse media.
High-risk jurisdiction exposure, offshore parent, or tax transparency concerns

Root cause: High-risk jurisdiction exposure, offshore parent, or tax transparency concerns

Defense evidence: Economic substance memorandum demonstrating management and decision-making in Spain, group organisational chart, tax residence certificates, certified financial statements, transfer pricing documentation under OECD principles, business contracts showing real operational activity, licensing and professional registrations applicable to fractional CFO advisory, and Form 720 declarations where applicable.
Sanctions, adverse media, or politically exposed counterparties in the trade payment chain

Root cause: Sanctions, adverse media, or politically exposed counterparties in the trade payment chain

Defense evidence: Automated EU/OFAC/UN sanctions screening results, negative news screening for all shareholders and contracting parties, list of client jurisdictions and counterparties with due diligence files, contractual warranties on non-sanctioned involvement, dual-use or export-control classification if services touch restricted sectors, and compliance committee approval memorandum.
Unclear source of funds for initial capital injection, shareholder loan, or subscription of new shares

Root cause: Unclear source of funds for initial capital injection, shareholder loan, or subscription of new shares

Defense evidence: Original bank transfer confirmation from the remitting bank, remitter's bank statements, audited financial statements of the shareholder, copy of the corporate resolution approving the capital increase, notarised deed of incorporation or capital increase, tax declaration evidencing income or dividend tax treatment, and an accountant's letter explaining the source of funds.
Multicurrency ledger inconsistencies or unverifiable cross-border accounting records

Root cause: Multicurrency ledger inconsistencies or unverifiable cross-border accounting records

Defense evidence: IFRS-compliant multi-currency general ledger, transaction-by-transaction reconciliation, intercompany agreement, invoices with full VAT and corporate tax trail, SWIFT MT103s for each inbound flow, FX confirmations, integrated accounting system extract in Spanish or English, and a statutory auditor's comfort letter when needed.

Cross-Border Clearing Corridors & Settlement Fit

Capital injections from foreign shareholders are executed by SWIFT MT103 or SEPA for euro-denominated transfers, using the Spanish SL's dedicated capital account in the name of the company at a tier-1 Banco de España supervised credit institution. The payment message should identify the company as beneficiary and reference the notarised capital increase deed. Before wiring, the bank requires the signed investor resolution, notarial deed of capital increase, registered UBO documentation, and Tax ID of the Spanish SL. The transfer is categorised as a direct investment in equity capital for balance-of-payments statistical purposes and must be reported to Banco de España when above the reporting threshold. Funds should not be passed through third-country intermediary wallets, cryptocurrency exchanges, or aggregated EMI virtual accounts. The bank will verify that the source of funds originates from a bank account in the name of the investor or from an audited group treasury, and any loan intermingling must be avoided to preserve clean equity classification.The primary clearing rails are SWIFT MT103 for urgent high-value single cross-border payments, MT202 for interbank cover if required, and SEPA Instant or SEPA Credit Transfer for euro-denominated intra-EU trade disbursements. Documentary trade settlements are executed through Commercial Letters of Credit issued under UCP600, standby letters of credit under ISP98, and independent guarantees under URDG758. For virtual CFO services, typical outbound treasury payments consist of subcontractor invoices, licensing fees, SaaS subscriptions, payroll, and professional fees; each must be supported by a matching invoice, contract, Irish? Malaga? No, by underlying service agreement and an FX conversion confirmation when the beneficiary currency differs. The financial institution must screen all payee names against sanctions and PEP lists before execution. The Spanish SL does not need exchange control approval, but the bank may require a copy of the invoice and, for large non-trade payments, the previously filed balance-of-payments declaration. Use of distributed ledger rails, personal payment cards, or peer-to-peer transfers is not acceptable for statutory disbursements.Outright FX forwards between EUR and freely convertible currencies, executed under ISDA or a Spanish master agreement with credit support annex and valuation marginFX swaps involving simultaneous spot and forward exchange of principal and interest in two currencies for temporary liquidity matchingCross-currency swaps with actual exchange of principal and interest to hedge long-term intercompany loans or capital exposureEuropean-style FX options and zero-premium collar structures to protect budgeted cash flows in USD, GBP, LATAM currencies, and emerging market currenciesForeign exchange swap agreements executed on regulated markets or with required disclosure of underlyingsNon-deliverable forwards permitted strictly where the underlying emerging or non-convertible currency cannot be settled deliverably in the EU and the nominal exposure is documented against a real commercial forecast

E-commerce / gateway settlement fit: Medium to High, subject to PSD2 and Banco de España supervision. EEA-authorised electronic money institutions and payment institutions can provide IBANs, multi-currency wallets, payout services and SWIFT-like rails through passporting, but they are not eligible substitutes for a statutory credit institution account when bank confirmation for capital increases or documentary trade credits is required. Cross-border EMIs such as Wise for business may serve payroll to foreign contractors, vendor disbursements, and collection waterfall accounts, but the primary corporate current account for tax, creditor protection, and SL statutory capital contributions should remain at a fully licensed credit institution. Any EMI arrangement must preserve segregated customer funds, include Spanish language and consumer protection disclosures, and cannot offer deposit-taking or credit products.

Statutory Filing Calendar

Statutory deliverableDeadline window Government feeDelinquency sanctions
Legalization of accounting books Within four months after the financial year-end; normally by 30 April for a 31 December year-end $30 USD Potential administrative penalties and evidentiary disadvantages; repeated non-compliance may contribute to registry compliance issues. No automatic strike-off solely for late book legalization.
Preparation and approval of annual accounts Directors must prepare accounts within three months after year-end; shareholders must approve them within six months after year-end $0 USD Director liability exposure and delayed statutory filing. Failure to approve accounts prevents timely registry deposit.
Deposit of annual accounts Within one month after shareholder approval; normally by 25 July for a 31 December year-end where approval occurs by 30 June $70 USD Registry closure may arise if accounts remain undeposited for one year after the filing deadline. Administrative fines generally range from EUR 1,200 to EUR 60,000, subject to statutory calculation rules; registry closure restricts registration of most corporate acts.
Ultimate beneficial owner declaration accompanying annual accounts Submitted with the annual accounts and updated whenever beneficial ownership information changes $0 USD Incomplete or inconsistent beneficial ownership information may delay or reject the annual accounts filing and may create anti-money-laundering compliance exposure.
Corporate income tax return, Modelo 200 Within the first 25 calendar days following the six-month period after financial year-end; normally 1 to 25 July for a 31 December year-end $0 USD Late filing without tax payable generally attracts a fixed penalty, subject to reductions. Where tax is payable, penalties are generally 1% plus 1% for each complete month of delay, with increased penalties after twelve months and late-payment interest.
Annual VAT summary return, Modelo 390, if applicable Generally filed from 1 to 30 January following the relevant calendar year, unless the taxpayer is exempt from the summary return under applicable VAT reporting rules $0 USD Late or omitted filing may result in fixed tax penalties, generally reduced for voluntary correction before tax authority assessment.

Box 1 - Taxable base Net taxable income before deductions and tax credits Non-residents report Spanish-source income only; claim DTA relief where applicable 100 EUR per day of delay (maximum 6,000 EUR), statutory interest on late payments, and potential criminal prosecution for evasion
Box 2 - Withholding taxes Withholding taxes paid or payable on Spanish-source income Deductible WHT on dividends, interest, and royalties; supported by payment certificates 100 EUR per day of delay (maximum 6,000 EUR), statutory interest on late payments, and potential criminal prosecution for evasion
Box 3 - Tax loss carryforward Offset of prior-year losses against current taxable base Limited to 50% of taxable base annually; carryforward subject to annual limits 100 EUR per day of delay (maximum 6,000 EUR), statutory interest on late payments, and potential criminal prosecution for evasion

Transfer Pricing & Economic Substance

Master / Local File threshold: 250,000 EUR (local file); 50,000,000 EUR group turnover (master file)

Economic substance scope: Spain applies ESR to entities in relevant activities (IP holding, distribution, financing, or certain services) where group thresholds are met; requires adequate local substance to support tax residency and benefits

Fatal Compliance Red Lines & Director Liability

Failure to file corporate tax return

Statutory sanction: Administrative fine of 100 EUR per day (max 6,000 EUR) plus interest and possible criminal liability

Director personal liability: Personal liability for tax debts; potential disqualification from management and criminal prosecution
Transfer pricing non-compliance

Statutory sanction: Tax reassessment of profits, fines up to 100% of additional tax due, and criminal sanctions

Director personal liability: Piercing the corporate veil; directors personally liable for restitution and possible imprisonment
Dividend withholding tax non-remittance

Statutory sanction: Fines equivalent to 100-500% of evaded WHT plus interest and criminal penalties

Director personal liability: Directors personally liable for unpaid WHT; subject to disqualification and criminal sanctions
Economic substance violation

Statutory sanction: Denial of benefits, back taxes, fines up to 500,000 EUR or more, and criminal prosecution

Director personal liability: Personal liability for tax liabilities; possible disqualification and imprisonment for fraudulent conduct
